claims.claim: A six-stop elevator costs about $170,000 to install in North America and $60,000 or less in Europe according to Stephen Smith.
claims.episode_span: A six-stop elevator that costs roughly one hundred seventy thousand dollars to install in North America can be put in for sixty thousand dollars or less across the Atlantic.
claims.supporting_quote: Smith estimates that a new six-stop elevator that costs $170,000 to install in North America would run $60,000 or less across the Atlantic.

claims.claim: The United States has 3.1 elevators per thousand residents while Switzerland has 27 and Spain has 23, per Stephen Smith.
claims.episode_span: Smith’s data show the United States has only 3.1 elevators per thousand residents compared with twenty-seven in Switzerland and twenty-three in Spain.
claims.supporting_quote: The U.S., according to Smith, has 3.1 elevators per thousand residents, while Canada has 4.1. By contrast, Greece has at least 41, Switzerland has 27, and Spain has 23.

claims.claim: New York developers budget $7,500 per year per elevator for maintenance while German firms quote around $450, according to Stephen Smith.
claims.episode_span: Maintenance contracts reflect the same pattern: New York developers budget seven thousand five hundred dollars a year per unit while German firms quote around four hundred fifty dollars.
claims.supporting_quote: budget $7,500 for annual elevator maintenance, with private housing operators in New York and Washington quoting similar numbers. This is several times European costs: one German firm, for instance, offers midrise maintenance contracts for about $450 per year.
